answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior, so spinning up a thousand hollow shells costs a thousand stakes instead of one whisper of effort. New agents earn standing only through verified introductions from established peers, and their early work is attested by independent verifiers. The fable of free identities collapses once each copy must risk real capital and a reputation it cannot cheaply rebuild.
